Delete $src and run the install" \\\n       "again for a fresh clone; /usr/local/bin/cyanrip and the host export" \\\n       "are UNCHANGED" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\necho "platterpus: tree is clean"\n# meson's vcs_tag resolves the build tag by running git in the source root. If\n# THAT cannot work, the tag silently becomes upstream's `release` fallback — the\n# v0.6.4b2 symptom — so probe it here, where a failure is attributable.\nif git -C "$src" rev-parse --short HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n  echo "platterpus: git is usable in the source root (vcs_tag should resolve)"\nelse\n  echo "platterpus: WARNING git is NOT usable in the source root — meson's" \\\n       "vcs_tag will fall back and the build tag will name no commit" >&2\nfi\n\n# `--wipe` reconfigures an existing build dir (and fails if there isn't one),\n# so branch on it rather than deleting anything.\necho "platterpus: meson options=${meson_opts:-(none)}"\n# Unquoted on purpose — see `meson_opts` above. `set -eu` is active, so an empty\n# value expands to nothing rather than to an empty argument.\n# shellcheck disable=SC2086\nif [ -d "$src/build" ]; then\n  echo "platterpus: reconfiguring existing build dir"\n  meson setup --wipe $meson_opts "$src/build" "$src"\nelse\n  echo "platterpus: configuring a fresh build dir"\n  meson setup $meson_opts "$src/build" "$src"\nfi\nninja -C "$src/build"\n\n# --- Read the banner off the thing we just built ----------------------------\n# The build step's own self-check. Previously the first time anyone learned the\n# banner was wrong was three commands later, in the verify step, which reported\n# only what it EXPECTED. Checking it *here* is\n# the whole point: the steps that follow are `sudo install` over\n# /usr/local/bin/cyanrip and `distrobox-export` over the host wrapper, and both\n# are irreversible. Verifying only after them means a failed check reports the\n# problem accurately and still leaves the wrong ripper on the ripping path,\n# with no rollback — the guard meant to be the last word running after the\n# point of no return.\n#\n# The post-install verify stays. Two checks are not redundant here: this one\n# says "we built the right thing", the later one says "the right thing is what\n# landed and got exported". A single check cannot cover both, because install\n# and export are exactly where a correct build could still go astray.\nif [ -z "$_banner" ]; then\n  echo "platterpus: FATAL the binary we just built answered none of: -V --version" >&2\n  echo "platterpus: refusing to install it — nothing has been changed" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\n# The tag must be the WHOLE parenthetical: `*"$5"*` alone also accepted\n# `($5-dirty)`, a binary that says itself it was built from a modified tree\n# (the claude-code-skills review of 2026-10-26, item 2.2).\ncase "$_banner" in\n  *"($5)"*)\n    echo "platterpus: built binary identifies as $5 — safe to install" ;;\n  *)\n    echo "platterpus: FATAL built binary reports \\"$_banner\\"" >&2\n    echo "platterpus: but commit $4 must produce build tag \\"$5\\"" >&2\n    case "$_banner" in\n      *"($5"[0-9a-f]*)\n        echo "platterpus: that is the right commit with a LONGER short hash" \\\n             "than the published tag; the source tree's git abbreviates it" \\\n             "differently, so the binary's tag would not match the pin" >&2 ;;\n      *"($5-dirty)"*)\n        echo "platterpus: that is a DIRTY build of the right commit — its own" \\\n             "tag says the tree it was built from had changes, so it is not" \\\n             "the published build" >&2 ;;\n      *-grelease*|*-gunknown*)\n        echo "platterpus: that tag names no commit at all — meson's vcs_tag fell" \\\n             "back to its literal default, so the binary cannot prove which" \\\n             "source built it" >&2 ;;\n    esac\n    echo "platterpus: refusing to install it — /usr/local/bin/cyanrip and the" \\\n         "host export are UNCHANGED, so the previously working ripper is still" \\\n         "in place" >&2\n    exit 1 ;;\nesac\n build-cyanrip-fork .cache/platterpus/cyanrip-fork https://github.com/rmccann-hub/cyanrip.git platterpus-fork 5cc1c6b platterpus-fork-g5cc1c6b  5cc1c6b3f6c8ea34d74a2f7672bdc5e6830ecbf0

The\n# fork's meson `vcs_tag` prints `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, and git sizes a\n# short hash by how many objects the repository holds: seven characters until\n# a clone passes about 16,000 objects, eight after. The fork's repository passed\n# that line with `.29`, so a reused clone built a tag ending `-g8d2ca726` where\n# the published build, and the pin, end `-g8d2ca72`, and the check\n# below refused a correct build (the owner's install of 0.7.120, 2026-11-04).\n# Seven, git's own floor, is what the fork publishes; git still lengthens a\n# prefix that is ambiguous, and the check below then refuses, which is right.\ngit -C "$src" config core.abbrev 7\n\n# --- Prove the tree is what we asked for, before building it ----------------\n# A build tag names a commit; it does not name what was built (CLAUDE.md rule\n# 12). So state the commit we actually landed on, REFUSE unless it is the one we\n# asked for, and REFUSE a dirty tree: a dirty tree bakes a tag for a different\n# tree, silently. Both refusals happen before anything is built or installed.\nhead="$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)"\necho "platterpus: HEAD=$head"\necho "platterpus: HEAD short=$(git -C "$src" rev-parse --short HEAD)"\necho "platterpus: describe=$(git -C "$src" describe --always --dirty 2>&1 || true)"\nif [ -n "$full" ]; then\n  if [ "$head" != "$full" ]; then\n    echo "platterpus: FATAL HEAD is $head but the pin $pin is commit $full" >&2\n    echo "platterpus: refusing to build — /usr/local/bin/cyanrip and the host" \\\n         "export are UNCHANGED" >&2\n    exit 1\n  fi\n  echo "platterpus: HEAD is exactly the recorded commit $full"\nelse\n  # No full commit recorded for this pin: the weaker check, said as weaker.\n  pin_lc="$(printf '%s' "$pin" | tr 'A-F' 'a-f')"\n  case "$head" in\n    "$pin_lc"*)\n      echo "platterpus: HEAD begins with $pin_lc (no full commit is recorded" \\\n           "for this pin, so only the prefix is checked)" ;;\n    *)\n      echo "platterpus: FATAL HEAD is $head, which does not begin with $pin" >&2\n      echo "platterpus: refusing to build — /usr/local/bin/cyanrip and the host" \\\n           "export are UNCHANGED" >&2\n      exit 1 ;;\n  esac\nfi\n# `git status --porcelain` lists changed tracked files and untracked ones that\n# are not ignored; `build/` is ignored at every pin we build, so a reused build\n# dir is not dirt. An untracked file can still change what compiles (a stray\n# header next to the sources), which is why it counts.\nif ! dirt="$(git -C "$src" status --porcelain 2>&1)"; then\n  echo "platterpus: FATAL could not read the source tree's status:" >&2\n  printf '%s\\n' "$dirt" >&2\n  echo "platterpus: refusing to build a tree whose state is unknown —" \\\n       "/usr/local/bin/cyanrip and the host export are UNCHANGED" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\nif [ -n "$dirt" ]; then\n  echo "platterpus: FATAL the source tree is DIRTY — the build tag would not" \\\n       "describe what is built:" >&2\n  printf '%s\\n' "$dirt" >&2\n  echo "platterpus: refusing to build it. Delete $src and run the install" \\\n       "again for a fresh clone; /usr/local/bin/cyanrip and the host export" \\\n       "are UNCHANGED" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\necho "platterpus: tree is clean"\n# meson's vcs_tag resolves the build tag by running git in the source root. If\n# THAT cannot work, the tag silently becomes upstream's `release` fallback — the\n# v0.6.4b2 symptom — so probe it here, where a failure is attributable.\nif git -C "$src" rev-parse --short HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n  echo "platterpus: git is usable in the source root (vcs_tag should resolve)"\nelse\n  echo "platterpus: WARNING git is NOT usable in the source root — meson's" \\\n       "vcs_tag will fall back and the build tag will name no commit" >&2\nfi\n\n# `--wipe` reconfigures an existing build dir (and fails if there isn't one),\n# so branch on it rather than deleting anything.\necho "platterpus: meson options=${meson_opts:-(none)}"\n# Unquoted on purpose — see `meson_opts` above. `set -eu` is active, so an empty\n# value expands to nothing rather than to an empty argument.\n# shellcheck disable=SC2086\nif [ -d "$src/build" ]; then\n  echo "platterpus: reconfiguring existing build dir"\n  meson setup --wipe $meson_opts "$src/build" "$src"\nelse\n  echo "platterpus: configuring a fresh build dir"\n  meson setup $meson_opts "$src/build" "$src"\nfi\nninja -C "$src/build"\n\n# --- Read the banner off the thing we just built ----------------------------\n# The build step's own self-check. Previously the first time anyone learned the\n# banner was wrong was three commands later, in the verify step, which reported\n# only what it EXPECTED. Reading it here attributes a wrong tag to the build\n# that produced it.\nbuilt="$src/build/src/cyanrip"\nif [ -x "$built" ]; then\n  echo "platterpus: built binary=$built"\n  _banner=''\n  for _f in -V --version; do\n    if _out="$("$built" "$_f" 2>/dev/null)"; then\n      _banner="$(printf '%s\\n' "$_out" | head -n 1)"\n      echo "platterpus: built banner=$_banner"\n      break\n    fi\n  done\nelse\n  echo "platterpus: FATAL ninja reported success but $built is not executable" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\n\n# --- REFUSE HERE, BEFORE ANYTHING IS INSTALLED ------------------------------\n# $5 is the build tag a correct build of $4 must print. Checking it *here* is\n# the whole point: the steps that follow are `sudo install` over\n# /usr/local/bin/cyanrip and `distrobox-export` over the host wrapper, and both\n# are irreversible. Verifying only after them means a failed check reports the\n# problem accurately and still leaves the wrong ripper on the ripping path,\n# with no rollback — the guard meant to be the last word running after the\n# point of no return.\n#\n# The post-install verify stays. Two checks are not redundant here: this one\n# says "we built the right thing", the later one says "the right thing is what\n# landed and got exported". A single check cannot cover both, because install\n# and export are exactly where a correct build could still go astray.\nif [ -z "$_banner" ]; then\n  echo "platterpus: FATAL the binary we just built answered none of: -V --version" >&2\n  echo "platterpus: refusing to install it — nothing has been changed" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\n# The tag must be the WHOLE parenthetical: `*"$5"*` alone also accepted\n# `($5-dirty)`, a binary that says itself it was built from a modified tree\n# (the claude-code-skills review of 2026-10-26, item 2.2).\ncase "$_banner" in\n  *"($5)"*)\n    echo "platterpus: built binary identifies as $5 — safe to install" ;;\n  *)\n    echo "platterpus: FATAL built binary reports \\"$_banner\\"" >&2\n    echo "platterpus: but commit $4 must produce build tag \\"$5\\"" >&2\n    case "$_banner" in\n      *"($5"[0-9a-f]*)\n        echo "platterpus: that is the right commit with a LONGER short hash" \\\n             "than the published tag; the source tree's git abbreviates it" \\\n             "differently, so the binary's tag would not match the pin" >&2 ;;\n      *"($5-dirty)"*)\n        echo "platterpus: that is a DIRTY build of the right commit — its own" \\\n             "tag says the tree it was built from had changes, so it is not" \\\n             "the published build" >&2 ;;\n      *-grelease*|*-gunknown*)\n        echo "platterpus: that tag names no commit at all — meson's vcs_tag fell" \\\n             "back to its literal default, so the binary cannot prove which" \\\n             "source built it" >&2 ;;\n    esac\n    echo "platterpus: refusing to install it — /usr/local/bin/cyanrip and the" \\\n         "host export are UNCHANGED, so the previously working ripper is still" \\\n         "in place" >&2\n    exit 1 ;;\nesac\n build-cyanrip-fork .cache/platterpus/cyanrip-fork https://github.com/rmccann-hub/cyanrip.git platterpus-fork e531a33 platterpus-fork-ge531a33  e531a33b1f4c7268a99b782136d6ceeae0da7946
